saints.name: St. Simeon of Jerusalem
saints.title: Bishop and Martyr
saints.shortBlurb: A kinsman of the Lord and second bishop of Jerusalem, who governed the mother church for decades and was crucified in extreme old age…
biography: Simeon was the son of Cleophas — the Clopas of the Gospel — and so a kinsman of the Lord, Cleophas being, as Hegesippus records, the brother of Joseph. After the martyrdom of James the Less, the surviving apostles and the kindred of the Lord met together and chose Simeon to succeed him as bishop of Jerusalem.

He governed the mother church of Christendom for many years. Before the siege, Eusebius relates, the Christians of Jerusalem, warned by a revelation, withdrew across the Jordan to Pella; and the church Simeon shepherded endured the destruction of the city in the year 70 and the long aftermath.

In the reign of Trajan he was denounced by certain heretics as a Christian and one of the line of David, and brought before Atticus the governor. After enduring torture for many days, at the age of a hundred and twenty he was crucified, about the year 107 — so Hegesippus relates, preserved by Eusebius — a wonder to all who saw his steadfastness.
saints.knownFor: Shepherding the church of Jerusalem after St. James.

sources.text: Eusebius, Church History (Book III; public-domain translation)
